aspects.says: With one base exception per module, a caller that catches a leaf it treats specially and the base for the rest handles a leaf added later without any change.
basis: section:Give a Module One Base Exception, So Each Caller Chooses How Finely It Catches

aspects.says: Catching Exception or RuntimeException instead of the module's base also turns a bug's NullPointerException into a business answer.
basis: section:Give a Module One Base Exception, So Each Caller Chooses How Finely It Catches

aspects.says: An API maps failures by an error-code field, never by message text, and returns its own text rather than the exception's message.
basis: section:Clients Branch on an Error Code, Never on the Message

aspects.says: A switch expression over the error-code enum with no default stops compiling when a constant is added; with a default, the new code falls to the fallback.
basis: section:Clients Branch on an Error Code, Never on the Message

aspects.says: Logging and rethrowing at each layer writes one record per layer for a single failure, multiplying alerts.
basis: section:Log an Exception Where It Is Handled, Never Where It Is Rethrown

aspects.says: An exception is logged once, with its stack trace, by the layer that handles it; lower layers add context to the exception they throw instead of logging.
basis: section:Log an Exception Where It Is Handled, Never Where It Is Rethrown

aspects.says: A rejection message gives the bad value, the accepted range and an identifier, so the log alone tells what was wrong.
basis: section:A Message Names the Bad Value and the Range It Expected, and Nothing Secret

aspects.says: Concatenating a whole request into a message copies every component (a record's toString() prints them all) into every log and ticket; secrets and personal data never go in a message.
basis: section:A Message Names the Bad Value and the Range It Expected, and Nothing Secret

aspects.says: IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException and UnsupportedOperationException are already mapped by existing handlers; a home-grown RuntimeException falls through to the fallback, while a subclass of the standard one keeps its meaning.
basis: section:Throw IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException or UnsupportedOperationException When They Already Mean the Error

aspects.says: IllegalArgumentException means the argument is wrong whatever the state; IllegalStateException means the argument is fine but the moment is wrong, and the choice decides what the client is told.
basis: section:Throw IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException or UnsupportedOperationException When They Already Mean the Error

aspects.says: A new unchecked leaf escapes a caller that catches the module's exceptions only by name; the code still compiles.
basis: section:Give a Module One Base Exception, So Each Caller Chooses How Finely It Catches
